workstream: harmonised (single input geometry) subset of the method-comparison table; see docs/METHOD_COMPARISON_PRESENTATION_PLAN_20260922.md

frozen_six_column_table.role: read-only reference; the harmonised subset also borrows its per-category region rectangle

extended_table.role: read-only; source of every protocol-leverage number in protocol_leverage.json

gate_definition: a column may join the harmonised subset only if it can emit one anomaly score map per test image together with the image ids (the same gate as the 2026-09-21 extension), and

its INPUT RULE can be set to the subset's rule - aspect-preserving resize with short side 448 - without changing model, weights, or post-processing semantics (a square *stretch* is a different rule and is therefore excluded), and
after the change it is still the published method (no newly invented variant).
region_rule: region = intersection of the participating rectangles AND of the frozen table's own region_rect for that (dataset, category), so every cell is directly comparable with Table 11/12 and the only remaining change is the input geometry

controlled_A1_J.basis: native: the controlled canvas is already short side 448 (s8_common_region.controlled_rect); per-image maps reused

controlled_A1_L.basis: same pipeline as controlled_A1_J: the second matching rule of the same controlled construction; per-image maps reused

anomalydino_canvas.basis: native: smaller_edge = 448 canvas (SPEED_VRAM_BENCH protocol column); per-image maps reused

anomalydino_canvas_rotation.basis: native: same input geometry as canvas (the 8-rotation augmentation only changes the reference bank); per-image maps reused

PatchCore_harmonised448.basis: official vendored PatchCore with only the dataset geometry changed: --resize 448 --imagesize 448, everything else identical to the official224 recipe

SubspaceAD_native_fp16.basis: its geometry is a square STRETCH (whole image resized to image_res x image_res, rect [0,1]^2), i.e. anisotropic sampling, not an aspect-preserving short side; mixing it in would add a second geometric difference
SubspaceAD_native_fp16.measured_evidence: smoke/subspacead_448.json - it DOES run at 448 on this card (btad/01, 2 query images: peak_gpu_mb 2433.5, token grid 32x32, 0.8181 s/img), so the exclusion is about the input rule, not about memory

WinCLIP_native_240.verdict: exclude - input rule + checkpoint bound to 240
WinCLIP_native_240.basis: transforms.Resize((240,240)) + CenterCrop(240) is the same square-stretch family, and the backbone is ViT-B-16-plus-240 with img_resize = img_cropsize = 240, so running at 448 would interpolate positional embeddings and no longer be the published checkpoint configuration
WinCLIP_native_240.not_run: no 448 run was attempted; the exclusion is code-level

AnomalyCLIP_zeroshot_518.verdict: exclude - input rule + transform bound to 518 + single zero-shot configuration
AnomalyCLIP_zeroshot_518.basis: official get_transform is Resize((518,518)) + CenterCrop(518) and the 37x37 patch grid belongs to that 518 checkpoint; it also has no seed/K loop, so it does not share the unit definition of the other columns
AnomalyCLIP_zeroshot_518.not_run: no 448 run was attempted; the exclusion is code-level

PatchCore_native_local128.basis: both frozen PatchCore columns are native configurations of the same method; under one input geometry they become one column. The 0.1000 macro pixel AP separating them is the protocol lever itself.

harmonised_run.units: 4 dataset groups x all 36 categories x seed 0 x K=1 = 36 category units (one quarter of the 144-unit full grid)
harmonised_run.input_geometry: aspect-preserving short side 448 for every member
